question.text: Antyodaya Seva Sangh, an NPO with listed ZCZPs, had its 12AB registration cancelled by the Income-tax Department on 15 May. The NPO's KMP did not file a 91(D) intimation within 7 days. Mr. Arjun Desai, SIA, is about to sign Form 3.1 on 10 June without having identified this non-disclosure. Which statement best reflects the SIA's obligation?

answer.text: The SIA has no duty to look beyond the NPO's filed disclosures - the non-filing is the NPO's problem.

The SIA should identify the 12AB cancellation during fieldwork, treat the non-disclosure as a material compliance deviation, report it in Form 3.1, and require the NPO's management to file a belated 91(D) intimation before sign-off.
The SIA should sign Form 3.1 as the 91(D) deadline lapsed and cannot be cured.
The SIA should resign the engagement as 12AB cancellation makes AIR filing optional.

explanation.text: The Logic: The SIA's AIR engagement must include compliance-check procedures covering 12AB, FCRA and 80G status plus all 91(D) filings during the year. Discovery of an undisclosed cancellation of 12AB (a material event affecting tax status and ZCZP investor protection) triggers both a qualification in Form 3.1 and a request for belated disclosure. Signing without addressing it is itself a professional lapse. The Trap: Option A abdicates SIA independence. Option C treats the deadline as terminal - while the SIA cannot cure 91(D), they can compel disclosure and report the delay. Option D misreads the regulatory trigger - 12AB cancellation doesn't abolish AIR obligation, it increases it. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/III-C tests auditors' duty on uncovered non-compliance; XXIII extends the same duty-to-qualify to SIAs on uncovered 91(D) non-disclosures. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Build a standing 'compliance triangulation' procedure: verify 12AB / 80G / FCRA current status from Income-tax / MHA portals directly, then reconcile to the NPO's own records AND to 91(D) filings. Any mismatch is a reportable deviation, not a soft finding.
